analyst_view.overall: Fifth-placed Como (26 points, WWWLW) host sixth-placed Juventus (21 points, six off the top four) on Sunday evening; the numbers lean slightly to Como, who have scored 16 in their last six. Cesc Fabregas is short up front: Moise Kean has a new tibia injury and is out for about two months (Fabregas, ESPN, Sky via JuveFC), Jesus Rodriguez is out until December, and Diao, Addai and Caqueret missed Tuesday's Champions League game with AEK, leaving Douvikas as the only fit senior striker. The numbers list no absentees for this match yet, but Kean has played only 160 league minutes for Como and has been out since early October, and Rodriguez since October, so Como's strong form was built without them. Luciano Spalletti's Juventus have long-term absentees too (Yildiz until mid-December, Thuram and Locatelli into 2027, Kalulu for two more weeks), also already reflected in their recent form, and they play Omonia in the Europa League on Thursday, three days before this game, while Nico Gonzalez is aiming to return. No referee is named yet, so I stay with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, 1.3 for Como. Como lose Kean and Jesus Rodriguez, but both have been out since October while Como scored 16 in six, which the numbers already count (+2.3%); Juventus have been without Yildiz, Thuram and Locatelli for weeks as well. I stay at about 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, 4.3 for Juventus, already nudged up for Juve's 44 corners in six. Como's possession game through Nico Paz, Da Cunha and Baturina is unchanged by the injuries up front, and Juve's wide play with Conceicao and Zhegrova continues, so I stay at about 9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already cut sharply because Como have been booked only 3 times in six games (-18.9%) and Juve 8. A top-six clash could be tighter than that run suggests, but no referee is named yet and there is no rivalry edge, so I stay at about 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.5 shots, 15.4 for Como, already raised for Como's shooting against a Juve side that has allowed 91 in six. Juve's Thursday Europa League game may bring some rotation, but Spalletti has said everyone will play in this run of games, so the effect is hard to size; I stay at about 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target, already lowered for Juventus's recent accuracy (-6.7%). With Douvikas as Como's lone fit striker, as in recent weeks, and Juventus still without Yildiz, nothing new points either way, so I stay at about 7.8.
